title: Short Stuff: Mesas: Flat
summary: Short Stuff episode on mesas, buttes, and plateaus. Josh recounts a birthday trip to Santa Fe, New Mexico, where he and his wife Emily saw flat-topped mountains on the drive from Albuquerque and wondered what they were. The hosts cover the etymology of "mesa" (Spanish for table, named by 16th-century Spanish explorers searching for the Seven Cities of Cibola), the French origin of "butte," the size-based distinction (wider than tall is a mesa, taller than wide is a butte), and the formation process: sedimentary rock capped by hard cap rock, erosion by water and wind, plateaus uplifted by magma pressure, and the role of flash floods and river canyon carving. They close with Santa Fe recommendations (Canyon Road galleries, restaurants Geronimo and Sazón).

segments.title: Santa Fe trip and introducing mesas
segments.summary: Josh describes a birthday weekend in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and seeing flat-topped mountains on the drive from Albuquerque. The hosts introduce the topic of mesas.

segments.title: Etymology and definitions of mesa and butte
segments.summary: Mesa comes from the Spanish word for table, named by 16th-century Spanish explorers searching for the Seven Cities of Cibola. Butte comes from French. A mesa is wider than it is tall; a butte is taller than it is wide.

segments.title: How mesas and buttes form
segments.summary: Mesas and buttes form from flat-topped sedimentary rock with a hard cap rock that resists erosion. Water and wind wear away the surrounding land over millions of years.

segments.title: Plateaus, flash floods, and canyons
segments.summary: A plateau is uplifted land, often by magma pressure, and is the precursor to mesas and buttes. Water on arid plateaus runs off fast and carves canyons. The hosts share a story of a sudden storm in the desert and water running uphill.

segments.title: Wrap-up and Santa Fe recommendations
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the topic and recommend Canyon Road galleries and the restaurants Geronimo and Sazón in Santa Fe, then sign off.
